subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw pursue same-user private-LAN reachability parity for gateway-host exec?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the missing diagnostic, but choosing to allow, block, or approve private-LAN exec traffic changes a security boundary and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping private-LAN access semantics unchanged and separately tracked.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent parity as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Policy Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and keep the behavior under the related private-network policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping private-LAN access semantics unchanged and separately tracked.

likelyOwner.reason: The exec runtime and host-routing history most consistently points to this owner for the policy call.
